items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Stanley has one and the guy playing guitar for Miles, for awhile, has one

ctx.x: Stanley Turrentine's Sugar. The title tune, Sugar? The last chord is mine. "Stanley, you can end like this, put this chord right here." And that's what we did. And the other record is Storm Flower, Jobim's record, because when I first met him during these sessions, I didn't know. I knew who he was but I never had met him. And not speaking any Portuguese, I was just kind of really over my head, verbally, you know. And he spoke enough English that I felt really silly, you know? So I said, "Mr. Jobim." He said,…
Wow. Do you find producers being very different in having an effect on what's happening? I'm thinking, Okay we've got a Creed here, we have a Orrin, we've mentioned over here …
